newsitem.title: USA: Qualcomm signs $300 mln, 4-year China pact.
newsitem.headline: Qualcomm signs $300 mln, 4-year China pact.

text.p: Qualcomm Inc said it signed a four-year agreement valued at more than $300 million with an affiliate of Telecom Great Wall Development Co of Beijing for the purchase of QUALCOMM-branded code division multiple access digital phones.
Starting in the second half of 1997, Telecom Great Wall was expected to initially take deliveries of Qualcomm's new 800 MHz, QCP-82O dual mode CDMA digital phones, it said.
Telecom Great Wall was expected to rapidly deploy commercial service to cities throughout China, it said.

"The explosive growth in China's wireless marketplace has created an increasing demand for high quality wireless services that only Qualcomm's CDMA digital technology can provide," said Paul Jacobs, president of QUALCOMM's Subscriber Products Division.
Headquartered in San Diego, Qualcomm develops, makes, markets, licenses and operates advanced communications systems and products based on digital wireless technologies.
